work_order.understanding:
Issue #108 collects nine follow-up findings the review and QA of PR #100 left open, all landing in packages/loot-core/src/shared/transactions.ts. The prior plan (v1) was rejected three times over and the critique round was empty again, so I re-derived the whole ticket against current main myself. Two of the three defects reproduce exactly as reported and are real product bugs: F1, a split whose legs are all deleted collapses to a row at the right amount with payee: null even though the leg being collapsed genuinely carried the payee; and F2, a survivor built by makeTransactionWithChildCategory reads the payee off only the FIRST promoted row, so a leg whose payee was deliberately cleared leaves the survivor payee-less even when another leg it absorbs carries one.

F4 does not reproduce, and this reverses both the previous arbiter and v1. difference is defined as parent.amount - sum(children), and promoting a leg of amount a changes the parent to parent.amount - a while changing the remaining children to sum - a, so (parent.amount - a) - (sum - a) equals the old parent.amount - sum: the figure is INVARIANT under promotion, by construction. I confirmed this three independent ways: the algebra; 90 surviving-parent promotions built the way the product builds them (splitTransaction -> addSplitTransaction -> updateTransaction per leg, which is the register's and the mobile editor's path, both funnelling through updateTransaction, which recalculates) across never-filled, half-typed, under-filled, exact, over-filled, opposite-sign and negative-expense patterns, of which ZERO carried a wrong Amount-left figure; and the symptom itself, difference: 12345 against an amount of 7345, traced to the test file's own makeOpenedSplit helper (transactions.test.ts:43), which builds the parent through splitTransaction -- whose error is computed as if the children totalled zero (transactions.ts:419) -- and then attaches children that already carry amounts, without ever recalculating. I drove both fixtures side by side: the helper's parent reports difference 12345; the identical split built the production way reports difference 500. F4 is a defect in the fixture, not in the code.

F7 remains false. On the #8207 conversion path makeChild hands the child the parent's payee as a DEFAULT (transactions.ts:67), so the promoted row already carries it and the ?? parent.payee fallback contributes nothing there -- v1's claim that the payee-original return comes purely through the fallback was wrong, and the rejection was right to say so. The fallback IS load-bearing, but only on a narrower shape: a sub carrying an explicit payee: null beneath a parent that keeps its payee, where the promoted row is null. I located that shape by driving it (a parent at 12345 that keeps payee-original, two subs both explicitly null, 1000 and 0, with the 1000 leg unsplit, so exactly one child remains and the promoted total falls short): today's code returns payee-original solely through the fallback, and F7's payee: data.payee ?? null returns null. That is the shape AC-3 must be pinned on; the #8207 shape the previous plan named passes whether or not the fallback exists and pins nothing.
work_order.root_cause: Two sibling construction sites build a surviving non-split row by spreading a split parent and overriding only the fields the reviewer happened to think of. splitTransaction (transactions.ts:414-423) moves a split's payee down onto its children by building the parent with payee: null, so every one of these rows inherits a null the parent's own spread supplies. (1) deleteTransaction's subtransactions?.length === 1 collapse (:377-386) overrides is_parent and error but not payee, so the collapsed row is payee-less even though the branch already holds the leg it is collapsing onto. (2) makeTransactionWithChildCategory (:110-131) resolves the payee from the single row passed in as data, which is only the FIRST promoted row -- while the survivor may absorb more than that one row, and any of them may be the only one carrying a payee. The two sites are the same defect twice; the second was repaired once already by PR #100 and the sibling was missed. (3) A third, separate matter: a parent surviving a partial unsplit keeps error from parentTransaction. The review called that stale, but difference is invariant under promotion by the algebra above, so it is correct; what is genuinely wrong there is only the fixture that manufactures the appearance of staleness. The shared rule is: a row rebuilt from a split must take its payee from the rows it absorbs, and never from the parent's null.
work_order.approach:
Two behaviour edits in transactions.ts, both about payee provenance, then the tests that must go red without them. I applied both as a prototype against current main and ran the suite beneath them, so every claim below is one I drove rather than one I inferred.

1. The delete-collapse (:377-386). The branch already holds the leg it collapses onto -- _subtransactions[0] -- so read the payee off it: `payee: _subtransactions[0].payee ?? rest.payee`. `??` is right rather than a scan because there is exactly one leg here. This is the one-line shape the reviewer proposed, and I confirmed it: today the collapse returns {id:'p', amount:12345, payee:null}, under the edit {id:'p', amount:12345, payee:'payee-parent'}.

2. The promoted survivor (:110-131 and its two call sites at :471 and :530). The fix is a THIRD PARAMETER, not a change to how `data` is read: makeTransactionWithChildCategory gains `promotedRows: readonly Partial<TransactionEntity>[]` and resolves `payee: promotedRows.find(t => t.payee)?.payee ?? parent.payee`. This is the point the rejection pinned and the previous plan got wrong in a way that would have shipped a half-fix. I proved the two rules are not interchangeable: on the reported shape (c1 5000 with an explicit payee: null, c2 0 carrying 'PAY', only c1 unsplit, so one child remains and the call site folds it in at :485-489), scanning newNonChildTransactions -- what v1 specified -- returns payee: null, the reviewer's symptom surviving the 'fix', while scanning nonChildTransactionsToUpdate returns payee: 'PAY'. The two call sites pass childTransactionsToUpdate and nonChildTransactionsToUpdate respectively, which is also what makes the scan self-documenting: it is the set of rows the survivor actually absorbs. I verified all 43 existing tests in transactions.test.ts stay green with both edits applied.

The `?? parent.payee` fallback STAYS. F7's claim that it is dead code is disproven, and the comment must stop asserting that a split parent's payee is always null. The fallback is what returns 'payee-original' on the explicit-null-sub shape I drove, and dropping it -- F7's remedy -- turns that survivor payee-less, reintroducing the exact defect this ticket exists to close.

F4 is NOT fixed, because it is not broken. I am not restating the review's arithmetic as a plan step; the invariance proof and the two runs that show the remedy moving nothing are in `evidence`. What ships instead is a test that pins the invariant on a faithfully built fixture, so the next reader who runs the existing makeOpenedSplit helper cannot mistake the fixture's stale parent for a code defect and open this a third time. That is a test-strength change and is scoped as one: it asserts behaviour that is already true, which is the honest description of it. The fixture must be built through updateTransaction, NOT through makeOpenedSplit -- on the helper the case would assert the manufactured 12345 and pass for the wrong reason.

Tests. Four cases beside the existing payee block (:950-1083). Two must be seen RED with the fix reverted; a third must be seen RED under its own specific sabotage (the fallback-drop for AC-3). The F4 case is deliberately green before and after; that is the point of it, and AC-4 says so rather than pretending otherwise.

files.change: Two behaviour edits plus a comment correction. (a) `deleteTransaction`'s `subtransactions?.length === 1` collapse (:377-386) gains `payee: _subtransactions[0].payee ?? rest.payee` beside its existing `is_parent: false` and `error: null` overrides, reading the leg already in hand. (b) `makeTransactionWithChildCategory` (:110-131) gains a third parameter `promotedRows: readonly Partial<TransactionEntity>[]` and resolves `payee: promotedRows.find(t => t.payee)?.payee ?? parent.payee`; its two call sites (:471 single-child early return, :530 delete-parent branch) pass `childTransactionsToUpdate` and `nonChildTransactionsToUpdate` -- the rows the survivor actually absorbs, the latter including the remaining child folded in at :485-489. The `?? parent.payee` fallback STAYS. The comment block at :118-128 is rewritten because the expression under it changes: it must explain that the survivor takes the payee of the first row it absorbs that carries one (which is not necessarily the row the category comes from), and it must drop its claim that the parent's payee is null on every path -- that claim is false, and I drove two live paths where a split parent keeps one. No exported signature changes; `makeTransactionWithChildCategory` is module-private.
files.why: Both confirmed behaviour defects are in this one file. Edit (b) needs the third parameter rather than a change to `data` because the row carrying the payee is not always the row `data` names -- I drove both candidate rules on the reported shape and they disagree there, which is precisely the shape the rejection named.

files.change: Add four cases beside the existing payee block (:950-1083). (1) F1: drive the real `deleteTransaction` through `splitTransaction` and a two-leg delete to the collapse, asserting the survivor carries the collapsing leg's payee. (2) F2: an under-filled split whose first leg is `5000` with an explicit `payee: null` and whose remaining leg is `0` carrying `payee-other`, unsplitting ONLY the cleared leg, asserting the survivor carries the remaining leg's payee. This is the shape that discriminates the two candidate rules, and the case must be built so it fails under a scan of `newNonChildTransactions` alone. (3) AC-3: a parent at 12345 that KEEPS a non-null payee beneath two subs both carrying an explicit `payee: null`, with one sub at 1000 and the other at 0, unsplitting the 1000 leg so exactly one child remains and the promoted total falls short -- the shape on which the fallback is load-bearing. Assert the survivor inherits the parent's payee, and record the case RED when the `?? parent.payee` fallback is dropped. (4) F4: a three-child split built the production way (opened through `splitTransaction`, each leg typed through `updateTransaction`) whose parent error is therefore recalculated, asserting that promoting a leg leaves the parent's new amount and its `difference` exactly as the arithmetic says. Do NOT build this case on `makeOpenedSplit`: on that helper the parent carries a manufactured 12345 and the case would pass while asserting the fixture's artifact. Each new case's red run is recorded per AC-6; case (4) is expected green before and after, and AC-4 says so explicitly.
files.why: F1, F2 and edit (b) each ship a behaviour change to a payee the register filters on, and each needs a case able to fail. Case (4) exists so the F4 rejection is recorded in the suite rather than only in this plan: without it the next reader runs `makeOpenedSplit`, sees `difference: 12345` against an amount of `7345`, and re-opens a fixed-by-nothing finding.

files.change: One-line `Bugfixes` note covering the user-visible half only: a transaction that stops being a split no longer loses its payee when a leg is deleted or unsplit. `authors` must be a real GitHub username -- the gate's identity denylist rejects `claude` and `github-actions` -- so the implementer sets it from the committing account. The note says nothing about 'Amount left:', because nothing about it is changing.
files.why: conventions.md: release notes are a hard gate and `git diff --diff-filter=AMR` means a PR touching none of these paths fails. The payee loss is user-visible; the F4 work is not, because there is none.

unsplitting a split whose first leg's payee was explicitly cleared, where the leg it absorbs carries one, still yields a survivor carrying that leg's payee (F2) — recorded RED with the fix reverted, and specifically RED under a scan of `newNonChildTransactions` alone, which is the rule v1 proposed and which I drove to return `payee: null` on this exact fixture

a parent that keeps a non-null payee beneath two subs both carrying an explicit `payee: null`, with one sub promoted so exactly one child remains, yields a survivor inheriting the parent's payee (AC-3) — recorded RED when the `?? parent.payee` fallback is dropped. The case must be built so that dropping the fallback changes the result; the #8207 shape where the sub merely OMITS `payee` does not qualify, because `makeChild` copies the parent's payee onto the child as a default and the case passes either way

the five pre-existing payee cases (never-filled, under-filled income and expense, single-child, opposite-sign) and `still returns each split-out row with its own payee` stay green with both edits applied — I ran this against a prototype: 43/43

acceptance.check: A split whose legs are all deleted collapses to a single non-split row carrying the legs' payee, rather than a row with `payee: null` at the right amount.

I drove it: today the collapse returns `{id:'p', amount:12345, payee:null}`, under the edit `payee:'payee-parent'`. Browser confirmation: open a 123.45 transaction under a payee you choose, Split it into 50.00 and 73.45, save, select both legs and delete them; the register shows one 123.45 row under that payee, not a blank one, and searching the register for that payee returns it.

acceptance.check: A survivor built from a split takes its payee from the rows it absorbs, not from the first promoted row alone: unsplitting a split whose first leg's payee was deliberately cleared yields a survivor carrying the payee of the leg it absorbs that has one.
acceptance.how_to_verify: The second new case, on the fixture the rejection specified and that I confirmed discriminates: first leg `5000` with an explicit `payee: null`, remaining leg `0` carrying `payee-other`, only the cleared leg unsplit, so exactly one child remains and the call site folds it in at transactions.ts:485-489. I drove both candidate rules on it: a scan of `newNonChildTransactions` alone leaves the survivor at `payee: null` (the reviewer's symptom surviving the fix), and a scan of `nonChildTransactionsToUpdate` returns `payee-other`. Note for the browser step, which cannot produce this state: clearing a leg's payee is reachable in the reducer but the register commits a split's legs as a group, so QA confirms AC-1 in the browser and treats AC-2's unit case as the evidence for the cleared-leg shape.

acceptance.check: The parent-payee fallback stays: on a parent that keeps a non-null payee beneath subs carrying an explicit `payee: null`, the survivor inherits the parent's payee instead of becoming payee-less.
acceptance.how_to_verify: The third new case, and it must be pinned on the shape where the fallback is load-bearing — which is NOT the shape the previous plan named, and pinning the wrong one pins nothing. On the #8207 conversion where the sub merely omits `payee`, `makeChild` copies the parent's payee onto the child as a DEFAULT (transactions.ts:67), so the promoted row already carries it and the case passes whether or not the fallback exists; I drove both variants and confirmed it. The load-bearing shape is a parent at 12345 that keeps `payee-original`, two subs both carrying an explicit `payee: null` at 1000 and 0, with the 1000 leg unsplit: today's code returns `payee-original` solely through the fallback, and F7's `payee: data.payee ?? null` returns null. Recorded so a future reader cannot re-derive F7's conclusion from the code and 'fix' it again, which would be a regression.

acceptance.check: Promoting a leg out of a split leaves the surviving parent's 'Amount left:' exactly equal to its new amount less the children still behind it — which, because `difference` is invariant under promotion, is the figure it already carried. No code change is made for this, and none is needed.
acceptance.how_to_verify: The fourth new case, on a fixture whose parent error is recalculated the way `updateTransaction` recalculates it — NOT on `makeOpenedSplit`, whose parent carries a manufactured error that no user can produce. On the three-child 12345 split with legs 5000/4345/2500 it asserts the surviving parent reads `amount: 7345, difference: 500`, and that 500 is the shortfall the split opened with, not a figure the promotion produced. I drove the two fixtures side by side: makeOpenedSplit's parent reports `difference: 12345` against an amount of 7345, and the identical split built the production way reports `difference: 500`. Browser confirmation is deliberately absent: there is nothing to observe changing, and the reviewer's symptom is reproducible only through the fixture. If QA does see 'Amount left:' disagree with the row on a partially unsplit split, that is a NEW finding — capture the exact figures and the leg amounts and attach them, because on every production-faithful fixture I could build the figure is correct.

acceptance.check: The leg promoted out of a split carries its own payee on the keep-parent branch, and a parent that survives a partial unsplit keeps `payee: null` because the register renders a split parent's payee from its children — the null there is correct and is not the defect AC-1 and AC-2 close.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Asserted by the three-child case. The second half is stated as a criterion because reviewer A explicitly asked for it to be recorded, so the next reader does not re-derive it from the code. I drove this shape: promoting a leg of a three-child under-filled split leaves the parent surviving with `payee: null` while the promoted leg carries its own — correct on both counts, and the reason the payee fix must not be applied to a surviving parent.

acceptance.check: Each behaviour change has been recorded failing with its own fix reverted, and the whole `transactions.test.ts` file is green with both edits applied.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Revert each source edit individually, run `yarn workspace @actual-app/core exec vitest --run src/shared/transactions.test.ts`, record the failing run for each, then restore. The third case needs its own sabotage rather than a source revert: drop the `?? parent.payee` fallback specifically. conventions.md requires the red proof; a green suite never seen red proves nothing. The F4 case is expected to pass in every configuration and AC-4 says so — it asserts behaviour that already holds, which is what makes it a record rather than a regression test. Baseline: I ran the file on current main before applying anything and it is 43/43 green, and 43/43 with both prototype edits applied, so a later failure is attributable.

acceptance.check: A release note exists under `upcoming-release-notes/` with a `Bugfixes` category, a real GitHub username in `authors`, and a one-line body.
acceptance.how_to_verify: conventions.md is explicit that a PR touching none of these paths fails the repository's own gate.

qa_script: AC-1: open a 123.45 transaction under a named payee, Split into 50.00 + 73.45, save, select both legs, delete both. Expect ONE 123.45 row still under that payee, not a blank one. Then search the register for that payee and expect the row in the result set.

AC-2: not reachable from the register — the cleared-leg state is a reducer state (see AC-2). Confirm instead that the ordinary split-out still returns each leg under its own payee: split 123.45 under a payee, retype one leg's payee to a different payee, unsplit both legs, and expect two rows under their own two payees.

AC-4: NO browser step. There is no user-visible change to 'Amount left:' — see AC-4. If you see 'Amount left:' disagree with the row on a partially unsplit split, that is a NEW finding: capture the exact figures and the leg amounts and attach them.
AC-5: in the AC-1 flow, confirm the surviving collapsed row shows the payee, and that before this change it rendered blank.
risks: The payee resolution rule is new behaviour, not a repair of one line: on a split whose legs carry DIFFERENT payees, the survivor takes the first absorbed row that has one, where today it takes the first promoted row's whether or not that row has one. I checked the six reachable shapes (never-filled, under-filled income and expense, single-child, opposite-sign, correctly-filled, retyped-legs) and every pre-existing case keeps its exact current value — the 43-test file is green under the prototype. Only the cleared-leg shape changes. A shape neither the review nor I thought of would need the same check.

I am contradicting a review finding (F4) that two reviewers, the previous arbiter and v1 all accepted, and shipping less than the issue asked for. That is a real cost: if I am wrong, this ships a smaller fix than the ticket wanted. My confidence rests on the algebra (the difference is invariant by definition), on 90 production-faithful promotions with zero wrong figures, on the fixture-artifact explanation confirmed by driving both fixtures side by side, and on both editors routing every leg edit through `updateTransaction`, which recalculates. The falsifiable version is cheap: the AC-4 case asserts the figure directly, so a future run either agrees or does not.

The clearest path to the reviewer's symptom is `makeOpenedSplit` itself, which will keep manufacturing a parent error no user can produce. A future test author may reasonably read it as a code defect. AC-4's case records the truth next to it. Fixing the helper instead is listed under `alternatives_considered` and rejected: it is load-bearing for five existing payee cases that are correct as written, and changing it would change what those assert for no behavioural gain.

F2's cleared-leg shape may not be reachable from the register UI, only from the reducer and the API. I confirmed the reducer accepts it; whether a user can commit it in a split editor I did not drive, and it is QA's to confirm. The unit case stands on its own either way -- it pins a rule the reducer must honour -- but the user-visible reachability of that rule is unverified.
The release note's `authors` field cannot be written until the committing account is known; conventions.md rejects `claude` and `github-actions` by identity denylist.
out_of_scope: F4 as a code change — the surviving parent's stale `SplitTransactionError`. It is not a defect: `difference = parent.amount - sum(children)` is invariant under promotion, and on every production-faithful fixture the figure is already correct. Recorded as AC-4's invariant test instead. If a real stale-figure report ever arrives, `packages/loot-core/src/server/transactions/merge.ts:167` is where to look first: it sets `is_parent: true` without recalculating, so a merged parent genuinely can carry an error that disagrees with its children. I confirmed that line exists and sets the flag without touching `error`. That is a different file, a different branch and not among the nine findings, so it belongs in its own ticket.

F5 — the scope-bookkeeping finding about files PR #100's diff touched that its work order did not name. Both are comment-only, the PR is merged, and correcting a merged PR's work order is not a change any runtime can make. This order names every file it touches, including the release note the previous one omitted.

F9 — the previous work order's AC-13 test-verification procedure was not performable as written (it depended on an under-fill state the editor will not commit). That is a defect in the old plan's text, not in the code. This order avoids reproducing it: AC-1's browser step is performable as written, and the shape that needed the impossible step is a unit fixture instead (AC-2).
F8 as a separate item — the reviewer states the fix it asks for is the same test F3 asks for; the three-child case covers both.

A target length for the rewritten comment at :118-128, and the length policy itself. F6 is a review comment about a comment, and `.sdlc/memory/patterns/planner-read-comment-wording-as-the-defect.md` records exactly what specifying that prose produces. The comment is being rewritten because the expression under it changes, and it must stop claiming the parent's payee is always null; how many lines it takes is the implementer's call.

Changing `makeOpenedSplit` (transactions.test.ts:43) to recalculate its parent error. It is the source of the F4 misreading, but the fixture is load-bearing for five existing payee cases that are correct as written, and rewriting it would change what those assert for no behavioural gain. AC-4 records the truth beside it instead.

The `?? parentTransaction` degenerate path at :530. Reviewer A could not reach it: `Account.tsx:1242` passes every child and `:1266` is guarded by `selectedChildTransactions.length === 0 -> continue`. Rewriting a guard for an unreachable branch is the speculative change this repo's review history argues against. With edit (b) the path is also harmless: an empty `promotedRows` yields no payee from the scan and falls through to the parent, which is what happens today.

Whether the collapsed row's CATEGORY should also come from the leg rather than the parent. The collapse keeps the parent's category, which is right because the surviving row IS the parent, and unlike the payee a split's category is not moved down onto the children — so there is no parallel argument forcing it either way. Left alone rather than widening the diff.
work_order.confidence_rationale: High on F1, F2 and the F4 disproof, because I did not take the proposal's or the reviewer's account for any of it: I drove each against current main myself, and then applied the two proposed edits as a prototype and ran the suite beneath them, confirming F1 flips from `payee: null` to the leg's payee, F2 flips from `payee: null` to `'PAY'`, and all 43 existing tests stay green. The F4 disproof is the claim most worth attacking, since it contradicts two reviewers and the previous arbiter, and it is not a judgement call but an identity — I confirmed it by algebra, by 90 production-faithful promotions with zero wrong figures, and by driving both fixtures side by side (makeOpenedSplit reports 12345 where the production-built split reports 500). I also drove both candidate payee rules and confirmed they disagree on the exact shape AC-2 names, which is what makes the third parameter necessary rather than stylistic, and I located the fallback's load-bearing shape myself after finding the previous plan's named shape passes with or without the fallback. What holds this below the high band: the payee scan is new behaviour on a field the register filters and sorts on rather than a one-line repair, though six reachable shapes are checked and the existing cases are unchanged; F2's cleared-leg shape is confirmed reachable only in the reducer and API, not in an editor; F4 is a negative claim, and a leg-edit path writing an amount without recalculating would reopen it — I enumerated the writers of `is_parent: true` outside tests, and the one that genuinely can leave a parent error stale (`server/transactions/merge.ts:167`) is named in out_of_scope rather than claimed as a finding; and the release note's author field is a hard gate I cannot fill from here. AC-6 requires the red-run record for each change, which is where I would rather the review push than in the triage.
evidence: F1 reproduced on current main. Driving the real `deleteTransaction` through `splitTransaction`: opened `{id:'p', amount:12345, payee:'payee-parent'}` with children c1=5000 / c2=7345, both legs carrying the payee; delete c1, then c2 -> `[{id:'p', amount:12345, payee:null, is_parent:false}]`. With edit (a) applied the same drive returns `payee:'payee-parent'`. The leg being collapsed genuinely carried the payee; the survivor loses it.

F2 reproduced, and the previous plan's rule shown insufficient by driving it. c1 = 5000 with an explicit `payee: null`, c2 = 0 carrying `'PAY'`, only c1 unsplit. Today the survivor is `payee: null`. Under a scan of `newNonChildTransactions` (what v1 specified) it is still `payee: null` — the leg carrying the payee reaches the survivor through `nonChildTransactionsToUpdate`, folded in at :485-489, not through the first promoted row. Under a scan of `nonChildTransactionsToUpdate` it is `payee: 'PAY'`. This is the shape the rejection asked to be pinned, and it discriminates the two rules cleanly.

F4 DISPROVEN — the surviving parent's error is invariant under promotion. `difference = parent.amount - sum(children)`; promoting a leg of amount `a` gives `(parent.amount - a) - (sum - a) = parent.amount - sum`, unchanged. Confirmed empirically by me: 90 surviving-parent promotions built the way the product builds them (`splitTransaction` -> `addSplitTransaction` -> `updateTransaction` per leg, the register's and the mobile editor's path) across never-filled, half-typed, under-filled, exact, over-filled, opposite-sign and negative-expense patterns — every 'Amount left:' figure correct, zero wrong.

F4's reported symptom traced to the fixture, by driving both. With `makeOpenedSplit` as written (transactions.test.ts:43) the parent reports `{amount: 7345, error.difference: 12345}` after promoting c1, because `splitTransaction` computes the error as if the children total zero (transactions.ts:419) and the helper then attaches children that already carry amounts. The identical split — 12345 into 5000/4345/2500, each leg typed through `updateTransaction` — reports `{amount: 7345, error.difference: 500}`, exactly the shortfall. The two runs differ only in whether the parent's error was recalculated at construction.

F7 DISPROVEN, with the evidence corrected to the shape where it actually holds. On the #8207 conversion with a sub that merely omits `payee`, `makeChild` copies the parent's payee onto the child as a DEFAULT (transactions.ts:67) and the parent keeps `payee-original`; the survivor comes back `payee-original` from the promoted row either way, so the previous plan's 'purely through that fallback' was wrong and a case pinned on it would pin nothing. The fallback IS load-bearing on a narrower shape, which I located and drove: a parent at 12345 keeping `payee-original`, two subs both at explicit `payee: null` (1000 and 0), the 1000 leg unsplit. Today's code returns `payee-original` solely through the fallback; with the prototype's fallback replaced by `?? null` the same drive returns `payee: null`. F7's remedy is therefore a regression on this shape, not a cleanup.

Prototype validated end to end, then reverted. I applied both edits, ran the existing file (43/43 green), and drove the probes beneath them. Then I sabotaged each rule in turn to confirm the cases discriminate: replacing `nonChildTransactionsToUpdate` with `newNonChildTransactions` at the :530 call site returns the F2 survivor to `payee: null`; replacing `?? parent.payee` with `?? null` returns the AC-3 survivor to `payee: null`. transactions.ts is restored byte-identical to its state on main (`git show origin/main:... | diff -` is empty), the probe file is deleted, and `git status --short` shows only the untracked `plan/` directory. Nothing was committed and nothing was posted.

Reachability checked for both payee sites. `Account.tsx:1242` passes every child and `:1266` is guarded by `selectedChildTransactions.length === 0 -> continue`, so the `newNonChildTransactions[0] ?? parentTransaction` degenerate path is not reachable from the app. Every writer of `is_parent: true` outside tests is accounted for: `shared/transactions.ts:351,419`, `server/accounts/sync.ts:49`, `server/tools/app.ts:84`, and `server/transactions/merge.ts:167` — the last sets the flag without recalculating, which is the one path that can genuinely leave a parent error stale, and it is named in out_of_scope.

Baseline: `vitest --run src/shared/transactions.test.ts` is 43/43 green on current main before any edit, and 43/43 with both prototype edits applied, so a later failure is attributable to the new cases.

The user-visible surface confirmed: `TransactionsTable.tsx:2350-2364` renders `error.difference` as 'Amount left:' behind `data-testid="transaction-error"` next to a `distribute-split-button`, and the mobile editor reads the same error at `TransactionEdit.tsx:334`. `recalculateSplit` (transactions.ts:132-146) is the only place the rule 'balanced means no error' is written.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep v1's F4 edit — recompute the surviving parent's error with `recalculateSplit({ ...parentTransaction, amount: <newAmount>, subtransactions: remainingChildTransactions }).error`.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes nothing, because there is nothing to fix: the difference is invariant under promotion, so the recomputed value equals the value already there. I ran 90 production-faithful promotions and found zero wrong figures, which is the case's own falsification test. It would also add code whose only observable effect is on a fixture no user can reach. Shipping it would mean a diff that looks like a money fix and is not, which is the specific shape `patterns/planner-read-comment-wording-as-the-defect.md` says this repo has been burned by.

alternatives_considered.approach: Apply F7 as written — drop the fallback to `payee: data.payee ?? null`, treating a split parent's payee as always null.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A regression, and I have the shape that proves it rather than the one v1 used. On a parent that keeps `payee-original` with an explicit `payee: null` sub beneath it, today's code returns the parent's payee through the fallback and F7's line returns null — reintroducing exactly the payee-less survivor this ticket exists to close. I drove it both ways. On the #8207 shape v1 cited, F7 happens to be harmless, but harmless on one shape is not a reason to delete a load-bearing fallback.

alternatives_considered.approach: Resolve the survivor's payee by scanning `newNonChildTransactions` (the previous plan's rule) rather than `nonChildTransactionsToUpdate`.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Correct on most shapes and wrong on the one that matters. When exactly one child is left behind, the call site folds it into `nonChildTransactionsToUpdate` (:485-489) and that folded-in leg can be the only one carrying a payee — the case the review reported. I drove both rules on that fixture: this one leaves the survivor at `payee: null`, which is the symptom. Scanning the rows the survivor actually absorbs fixes it; narrowing to `newNonChildTransactions` would have shipped the reviewer's bug still half-open while AC-2 claimed it closed.

alternatives_considered.approach: Change how `data` is read inside `makeTransactionWithChildCategory` rather than adding a third parameter.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `data` is the row the CATEGORY comes from and the caller already computes it as the first promoted row; the row that carries the payee is not always that row, which is the whole defect. Changing what `data` means would silently couple category provenance to payee provenance at both call sites and leave the degenerate path (:530, where `data` is the parent) reading a parent's payee as if it were a promoted row's.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix `makeOpenedSplit` (transactions.test.ts:43) so it recalculates its parent's error, removing the fixture that manufactured the F4 symptom at its source.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Tempting and wrong for this ticket. The helper is load-bearing for five existing payee cases that are correct as written, and changing what the parent carries would change what those cases assert for no behavioural gain. The fixture is a test-authoring hazard, not a defect; AC-4's case records the truth beside it, which is the proportionate response. Repairing the fixture itself is a clean standalone change with its own red-run record.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave F4 out of scope entirely, as reviewer A suggested ('worth a follow-up issue').
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Reviewer A's suggestion was reasonable given the evidence, and the evidence was wrong. Dropping it silently would leave the same false belief in the codebase that produced this ticket, and the next person to read `makeOpenedSplit`'s output would file it again. Recording the disproof as a test costs one case and ends the cycle.

alternatives_considered.approach: Take every finding at face value, including the comment-length trim as its own change with a specified length and the scope-bookkeeping finding as work.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: F5 is bookkeeping on a merged PR, not a defect, and `patterns/planner-read-comment-wording-as-the-defect.md` is the recorded shape of that mistake. F9 is a defect in the previous order's text, not in the code; this order avoids repeating it rather than editing the old plan. The comment is being rewritten regardless because the expression beneath it changes and it must stop asserting the parent's payee is always null — but specifying how many lines it should be is transcribing a review comment into an acceptance criterion, which is what that pattern file warns produces.

assumptions: The register's and the mobile editor's split state is always the output of `updateTransaction` / `splitTransaction` / `addSplitTransaction` / `deleteTransaction` in `shared/transactions.ts`, never hand-built. I enumerated every writer of `is_parent: true` outside tests and both editors route leg edits through `updateTransaction`, which recalculates the parent. A path I did not find that writes a leg's amount without recalculating would reopen F4 — this is the assumption the AC-4 case is designed to catch.

Reading the payee off the collapsing leg in `deleteTransaction`, and preferring the first absorbed row that carries one in `makeTransactionWithChildCategory`, is the right provenance. The alternative — that removing a leg should leave the survivor payee-less — has no support in the code, and the surviving row carries the whole split's amount, so the split's payee belongs on it. A judgement, not something I proved; the six reachable shapes are enumerated in `risks` and each was checked.

For a parent that survives, `payee: null` is correct and must not be 'fixed'. The register renders a split parent's payee from its children, so a surviving parent that is still a parent has nothing to render from itself. Reviewer A asked for this to be stated and it is AC-5.
The `promotedRows` parameter defaults to `[data]` so the degenerate :530 path keeps today's behaviour with no caller obliged to pass it — a convenience for the implementer, not a semantic claim.
unknowns: Whether a user can commit a cleared-leg split (`payee: null` on one leg) from the register's split editor. The reducer accepts it and I drove `updateTransaction` returning a cleared leg, but the editor saves a split's legs as a group and I did not drive the UI. If it is unreachable there, AC-2's rule is still correct for the reducer and the API, and its unit case still pins it; what would be unverified is the user-visible reachability, which AC-2's note already says.

Whether `merge.ts:167` genuinely produces a visible wrong 'Amount left:'. I confirmed it sets `is_parent: true` without recalculating the error, and that a merged parent can therefore carry an error disagreeing with its children, but I did not build the merge scenario end to end. It is out of scope here and named rather than claimed as a finding.

Whether the collapsed row's inherited `is_parent: false` + parent category combination has any rendering consequence not checked here. I asserted the payee because that is the reported defect and did not audit the collapsed row's other fields.
work_order.debate_summary:
There was no critique to judge: `plan/critique.json` is empty (`{}`) for the second run running, so round 2 produced nothing and every judgement below is mine, made against the code and by driving the probes myself. I largely kept the proposal's triage — it is unusually well evidenced, and I confirmed its behavioural claims, its disproof of F4 and its account of which caller-side list the payee scan must read independently rather than on trust — but I changed one thing and sharpened two.

The big call is accepting the reversal of F4. The previous arbiter kept F4 and changed only its remedy, and the critic who rejected that plan did not dispute F4's reality either; both took the stale figure as given. I think it is not given. `difference = parent.amount - sum(children)`, and promoting a leg subtracts the same `a` from both terms, so the figure cannot move. I checked that three ways — the algebra, 90 promotions built exactly the way both editors build them, and the two fixtures driven side by side, where `makeOpenedSplit`'s parent reports 12345 and the production-built split reports 500 for the identical split. I record this as a correction of the council's reasoning, not as a dismissal of its care: the previous arbiter was right that the naive remedy is wrong and right to prefer reusing the existing rule over widening a shared type. Both instincts were sound and are moot, because there was nothing to recompute. I flag it plainly because it ships less than the issue asked for on the strength of my own arithmetic, and AC-4 makes it falsifiable by the same suite this work order ships.

What I changed: the AC-3 shape. The proposal names the right principle — the fallback must be pinned where it is load-bearing, not on the #8207 shape where `makeChild`'s default makes it moot — but its own test case is described loosely enough that an implementer could build it on a fixture that passes with or without the fallback, which is the precise failure that killed the previous plan's AC-3. I drove both variants to find this: the #8207 shape where the sub omits `payee` comes back `payee-original` whether the fallback exists or not, while the explicit-`payee: null` shape returns `payee-original` today and `null` under F7's remedy. I pinned the numbers into files[] and AC-3 so the case cannot be built on the wrong shape.

What I sharpened rather than changed: I confirmed by driving both rules that scanning `newNonChildTransactions` returns the F2 survivor to `payee: null` while scanning `nonChildTransactionsToUpdate` returns `'PAY'`, which is the discrimination AC-2 needs to be worth writing; and I confirmed the prototype leaves all 43 existing tests green, which is the baseline AC-6's red-run record is measured against.

Where I expect pushback, honestly: the payee rule is new behaviour on a field the register filters on, and two of its premises — that a collapsing leg is the survivor's payee provenance, and that a split parent keeping a non-null payee is a live state — are judgements the code supports but does not settle. The cleared-leg state is confirmed reachable in the reducer and not, so far, in an editor. And F4's disproof is a negative claim resting on an enumeration of the writers of `is_parent: true`; I checked all of them, but a path that writes a leg's amount without recalculating would reopen it, which is why AC-4 asserts the figure rather than merely restating it.

On the route: the pre-assigned route is plan -> implement -> review -> qa, and it is right. Both defects reproduce deterministically in the reducer with no browser, and the one change that is new behaviour rather than a repair is exactly what review is for. No stage is missing, so I request none.
residual_risks: The payee resolution rule is new behaviour on a field the register filters and sorts by: on a split whose legs carry different payees, the survivor's payee can change where today it does not. Six reachable shapes were checked and every pre-existing case keeps its value, but an unconsidered shape would need the same check. Go here first if QA finds a survivor under the wrong payee.

The F4 disproof contradicts two reviewers, the previous arbiter and v1. If it is wrong, this ships less than the issue asked for. AC-4 asserts the figure directly on a faithfully built fixture, so the claim is falsifiable by the same suite this order ships.
`makeOpenedSplit` remains as written and will keep manufacturing a parent error no user can produce; a future test author could still read it as a defect and re-open F4 a third time.

`server/transactions/merge.ts:167` genuinely can leave a parent error stale, but this order does not fix it and its reachability is unproven. If a real 'Amount left:' report arrives, that is where to look.
The cleared-leg shape (F2) is confirmed reachable only in the reducer and API, not in an editor; if no user can reach it, AC-2 pins a rule without a user-visible symptom behind it.

No e2e test is added. Per qa/environment.md e2e is not in this pipeline's CI and `yarn typecheck` does not cover it, so the browser confirmation is QA's step and nothing in CI would catch a regression there.
The release note's `authors` value cannot be written until the committing account is known; conventions.md rejects `claude` and `github-actions`.

history.action: route plan -> implement -> review -> qa (model, confidence 85)
